component.name: PC GamePak
component.summary: Turn removable storage into physical game cartridges

description.p: PC GamePak turns a removable drive into a game cartridge. Plug it in and a launcher opens showing the cover art and the games on it. Nothing runs on its own: the window waits for you to press Play.

A cartridge is an ordinary exFAT drive with one small file at the root, so the same cartridge works on Windows and Linux without conversion. Games can live on the cartridge itself or be a link to one already installed through Steam, Heroic, GOG or Epic.
The wizard writes cartridges: pick a drive, pick games, pick artwork.
Cartridges are mounted by your desktop. If yours does not mount removable drives on its own, install and run something like udiskie, or nothing will appear when you plug one in.

description.p: A tap of an NFC card or a barcode scan can pick any game, including one on another PC that starts there and streams with Moonlight when you press Play. Emulated games can be made into cartridges that carry their ROM. The memory card is drawn as a card, with its saves round it, and the app and wizard have new icons that read at taskbar size.

Saves, playtime and compiled shaders now travel on the cartridge itself, so a game carries its progress between machines. New cartridges are formatted NTFS by default, because exFAT cannot hold the symlinks a Proton install is built from; the picker now offers eight formats and says what each one costs. A cartridge can open in the Steam Deck's home screen instead of the launcher's own window, and eject now names whatever is still using the drive before taking it away. A drive can be a memory card that carries only saves, or a cartridge can be both.
Packaging only: the Flatpak build, and autostart through the Background portal instead of a systemd user unit.
